from retry import should_retry

def test_should_retry():
    # status None
    assert should_retry(None, 'timeout') == True
    assert should_retry(None, 'connection') == True
    assert should_retry(None, 'unknown') == False
    assert should_retry(None, '404') == False  # error is string
    # status 429
    assert should_retry(429, None) == True
    # 5xx
    for s in range(500, 600):
        assert should_retry(s, None) == True
    # 4xx other
    for s in range(400, 500):
        assert should_retry(s, None) == False  # includes 429? 429 is 429 not in 400-499? 429 is in 400-499 yes, but spec says retry status 429 and all 5xx; never retry other 4xx. So 429 should be true even though 4xx range includes 429. Our logic handles 429 before 4xx check.
        # 429 already caught earlier, fine.
    # other statuses
    assert should_retry(200, None) == False
    assert should_retry(300, None) == False
    assert should_retry(100, None) == False
    # edge: status None with 4xx error string not timeout/connection
    assert should_retry(None, '404') == False
    # error None with 429
    assert should_retry(429, None) == True
    # error None with 500
    assert should_retry(500, None) == True
    # error None with 400
    assert should_retry(400, None) == False
    # error None with 599
    assert should_retry(599, None) == True
    # status None with error None
    assert should_retry(None, None) == False  # unknown error

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_should_retry()
